ut_cache_valley.blurb: This broad valley in northern Utah, spilling into southeast Idaho, lies between the Wellsville Mountains and the Bear River Range, with the town of Logan at its center. Sport climbing makes up about two thirds of the climbing, backed by a sizeable bouldering scene and a smaller share of trad and top-rope. Roped grades cluster from 5.10 to 5.13, with the biggest bulge around 5.11 and 5.12 and a fair number of easier lines; boulder problems run from V0 into the double digits but mostly sit at V0 to V5. Logan Canyon holds the great majority of the climbing, followed by Blacksmith Fork Canyon and Green Canyon. The crags in the main canyon are limestone with some quartzite. It turns cold in winter, though the walls catch sun, and ice climbing takes over for the season.

ca_fairview_mountain.blurb: Fairview Mountain rises out of the High Desert near Apple Valley, California, at roughly 3,800 feet, in a secluded setting. The rock is monzonite with a well-developed patina. Sport routes account for about half of the climbing, bouldering is a close second, and there is a modest amount of trad plus a few top-ropes. Lines are short to mid-length, roughly 25 to 90 feet. Roped grades concentrate between 5.9 and 5.11, peaking at 5.10 and topping out at 5.12; boulder problems are mostly V0 to V5, with a thin tail of hard ones into V11. The larger zones are Foreplay Area, Middle Earth, Tatooine and Land of the Lost, reached on foot by a hillside trail from the parking area, a walk of about 10 to 30 minutes depending on the zone.

co_north.blurb: This northern stretch of the Flatirons sits above Boulder, Colorado, on the east slope of Green Mountain at roughly 6,900 feet. The rock is hard, pebbly conglomerate sandstone of the Fountain Formation, tilted into big slabs. Trad leads the way, with a large bouldering scene beside it and a small amount of sport and top-rope. Grades cover nearly everything from 5.0 to 5.14, with plenty of moderates and a strong group in the 5.10 to 5.12 range; boulder problems run V0 to V10, mostly in the easier half. Routes range from short, newer sport lines to long slab climbs of many pitches. The main zones are the First through Fifth Flatirons, Skunk Canyon, Gregory Canyon with its Amphitheatre, and the Satellite Boulders, which hold the largest number of problems.

tn_obed_clear_creek.blurb: Where Clear Creek meets the Obed River on the Cumberland Plateau, sandstone cliff bands hold some of the best sport climbing in the Southeast. The rock is steep and often overhanging, with sedimentary layering that builds big horizontal roofs, jugs and slopers; it is hard and offers good friction. Sport routes lead, with a strong bouldering scene and a smaller trad contingent. Roped grades run mostly from 5.10 to 5.12, with a solid group at 5.13 and few easy lines; boulder problems span V0 to V11. Expect high first bolts, so a stick clip is handy. The big zones are Lilly Boulders, North Clear Creek, South Clear Creek, Little Clear Creek, Lilly Bluff and Middle Obed. Climbing goes on year-round, chasing shade or sun depending on the season.

ca_valley_north_side.blurb: Running mostly along Northside Drive on the north wall of Yosemite Valley, this area is granite and the climbing is overwhelmingly trad. Alongside it sit a large bouldering scene, a handful of aid routes and only a little sport. Routes range from short cracks and slabs to full big walls. Roped grades spread from 5.4 to 5.14 with the heaviest weight at 5.10 and 5.11; boulder problems are mostly V0 to V5 and reach V13. The largest sub-areas are Camp 4 Area, Yosemite Falls Area, El Capitan and Royal Arches Area. The valley draws climbers from around the world, so it is busy, and mild weather is part of the appeal.

wa_bouldering_in_icicle_creek.blurb: Icicle Creek winds up a canyon west of Leavenworth in the Central-East Cascades, and this is the area's all-bouldering collection. The stone is granitic, and the area ranks among the best bouldering in the state. Hundreds of problems lie close to the road beside pullouts, with more on boulder-filled plateaus on the north side of the canyon and riverside highballs. Grades span V0 to V12, with the greatest numbers from V0 to V5 and a long tail of harder ones. Mad Meadows, Forestland Boulders, Straightaway Boulders and The Sword/Underwear Rock are the big zones. Spring and fall tend to give the best conditions; summer is shady in the woods, and fall brings sun-warmed plazas.
